newsitem.title: INDIA: India SBI staff to widen strike on June 19.
newsitem.headline: India SBI staff to widen strike on June 19.

text.p: Officers' association of State Bank of India (SBI), India's biggest commercial bank, has called for a strike at 13 regional headquarters on June 19, officials said on Tuesday.

The strike, currently confined to the western states of Maharashtra and Goa, will be extended following the failure of talks between the SBI Officers Federation and the management on Monday, a bank official said.

The strike began on June 12 at the Bombay office to protest against the suspension of three officers accused of failure to follow procedures in handling accounts of CRB Capital Markets, a finance company now facing liquidation proceedings.
SBI's board is meeting in Calcutta on June 19 to finalise accounts for the year ended March 31, 1997.
The bank official said the strike would be extended to the bank's countrywide branches on June 23 if the dispute continues.
The inter-bank call market has not felt the pinch of SBI's strike because of good liquidity but the position may change next week because of large fund flows from banks, dealers said.
Payment for a 20.0 billion 7-year paper to be auctioned on Tuesday evening will be on Wednesday. Tax outflows from corporate accounts with banks this week will also add to the pressure, dealers said.
